newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali communists register bid to assume power.
newsitem.headline: Nepali communists register bid to assume power.

text.p: Nepal's main communist party and two allies formally staked a claim to power on Monday, and the centrist Nepali Congress party said it appeared to lack the votes needed to continue ruling the Himalayan kingdom.

Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) general secretary Madav Kumar Nepal and Lokendra Bahadur Chand of the centrist Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) registered their joint claim at the gates of King Birendra's palace at 11:35 a.m. (0550 GMT), witnesses said.

The communist and RPP leaders were accompanied by Gajendra Narayan Singh, leader of the Nepal Sudbhavana Party (NSP). Both the RPP and NSP had supported the Nepali Congress-led government that resigned after losing a confidence vote last week.
The UML leader told Reuters outside the palace that his party and its allies controlled 103 of 205 seats in the lower house of parliament, and would support the RPP's Chand as the new prime minister.
"We have produced 103 signatures supporting Chand," Nepal said.

Nepali Congress officials said their plan to stake a claim appeared in trouble. "I think we cannot form the government," Chakra Prasad Bahtola, tourism minister in the caretaker cabinet, told Reuters. "They (RPP) have crossed over."
